```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4, out.width = "100%")
has_stan <- crywolf:::.has_cmdstan()   # the model fit runs only with CmdStan
```

A classifier such as BirdNET (Kahl et al., 2021) lists detections: for each
audio file, the time windows where it found a species, with a confidence
score. An occupancy model needs something else: one row per sampling
occasion, including the occasions where nothing was found, and a separate
record of which detections a person checked. This article goes from the
first to the second with `fp_read_birdnet()`, `fp_read_validation()`, and
`fp_aggregate()`, and fits the model to the result.

The example data are made up so that the article runs anywhere, but they
have the layout of real files: BirdNET selection tables in the Raven format,
and the clip-by-clip verdicts written by the 'sheepdog' package
(https://provetelab.org/sheepdog/), which cuts clips from BirdNET detections
for review and is installed from the same R-universe as crywolf
(https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev).

## Two kinds of checking

Two designs use checked data, and they need different files.

* In the **observation-confirmation design** (Chambert et al., 2015), a
  person listens to clips that the classifier flagged and says whether each
  holds the species. The verdicts refer to detections, so they enter as
  counts of confirmed true and false detections per occasion. This is what
  `fp_read_validation()` and the `validation` argument of `fp_aggregate()`
  produce.
* In the **multiple-methods design** (Miller et al., 2011), a person
  annotates whole recordings, whether or not the classifier flagged them.
  These are a second detection method, entered as the `verified` table of
  `fp_data()`. In 'sheepdog', clips of whole recordings
  (`sampling_mode = "random_recordings"`) are of this kind and must not be
  passed to `fp_aggregate()`.

Either way, the clips must be chosen without regard to the classifier's
score. Clips picked because they have the highest scores contain fewer false
positives than the average detection and make the false-positive rate look
lower than it is. In 'sheepdog', draw them at random among the detections
(`sampling_mode = "random_detections"`).

## Example files

We start from a simulated dataset with known structure: 60 sites, each
recorded on 8 nights, with observation confirmation on about 40% of the
occasions.

```{r simulate}
library(crywolf)
sim <- simulate_fp(nsite = 60, nocc = 8, frac_confirmed = 0.4,
                   frac_verified = 0, seed = 1)
truth <- sim$data$auto
truth$file <- sprintf("S%02d_202401%02d_200000.wav", truth$site, truth$occasion)
head(truth[, c("site", "occasion", "file", "y", "n_true", "n_false")])
```

From it we write what the field data would look like. Each occasion with a
detection gets a BirdNET row with a high confidence, and some occasions
without one get a row below the threshold of 0.5 that we will use. One
selection table per site goes into a folder.

```{r write-tables}
set.seed(2)
dir_tables <- file.path(tempdir(), "birdnet")
dir.create(dir_tables, showWarnings = FALSE)
low <- truth$y == 0 & stats::runif(nrow(truth)) < 0.2
det <- truth[truth$y == 1 | low, ]
det$confidence <- ifelse(det$y == 1, stats::runif(nrow(det), 0.5, 1),
                         stats::runif(nrow(det), 0.1, 0.5))
det$start <- 3 * sample(0:199, nrow(det), replace = TRUE)
purrr::walk(split(det, det$site), function(d) {
  tab <- data.frame(
    Selection = seq_len(nrow(d)), View = "Spectrogram 1", Channel = 1,
    `Begin Time (s)` = d$start, `End Time (s)` = d$start + 3,
    `Begin Path` = file.path("/audio", d$file), `File Offset (s)` = d$start,
    `Species Code` = "compau", `Common Name` = "Common Pauraque",
    Confidence = round(d$confidence, 4), check.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.table(tab, file.path(dir_tables, sprintf("S%02d.BirdNET.selection.table.txt",
                                                       d$site[1])),
                     sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
})
list.files(dir_tables)[1:3]
```

The verdicts follow the layout of `validation_by_clip.csv`: one row per
reviewed clip. A confirmed occasion contributes one positive clip if the
species was there and one negative clip if the classifier also fired on
something else.

```{r write-validation}
conf <- truth[!is.na(truth$n_true) & truth$y == 1, ]
clips <- rbind(
  data.frame(conf[conf$n_true > 0, c("site", "file")], verdict = "positive"),
  data.frame(conf[conf$n_false > 0, c("site", "file")], verdict = "negative"))
clips <- merge(clips, det[, c("file", "start", "confidence")], by = "file")
validation <- data.frame(
  site = sprintf("S%02d", clips$site), species_code = "compau",
  source_audio = file.path("/audio", clips$file), clip_start = clips$start,
  clip_end = clips$start + 3, confidence = clips$confidence,
  sampling_mode = "random_detections", occasion_id = sub("\\.wav$", "", clips$file),
  verdict = clips$verdict)
f_validation <- file.path(tempdir(), "validation_by_clip.csv")
utils::write.csv(validation, f_validation, row.names = FALSE)
table(validation$verdict)
```

## Reading the files

`fp_read_birdnet()` reads every selection table in the folder, standardizes
the column names (`Begin Time (s)` becomes `begin_time`), and adds the name
of the audio file and, when the file name carries a `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS`
stamp, the time of each detection.

```{r read-birdnet}
detections <- fp_read_birdnet(dir_tables)
head(detections[, c("file", "start", "species_code", "confidence", "time")])
```

`fp_read_validation()` reads the verdicts, in the format of 'sheepdog' 2.0.0
or in the Portuguese format of the sampler up to version 1.2.0
(`validacao_por_clipe.csv`), and returns `TRUE` for a positive clip, `FALSE`
for a negative one, and `NA` for a clip not reviewed.

```{r read-validation}
verdicts <- fp_read_validation(f_validation)
head(verdicts)
```

When 'sheepdog' wrote the whole survey with `export_occupancy_data()`,
`fp_read_sheepdog()` reads that folder instead: every occasion, the
predictions, the reviewed clips with their sampling design, and the
recordings annotated by ear, already in the forms used below. It drops
clips drawn with `sampling_mode = "top"`, which were chosen for their high
scores, and refuses schemas it does not know.

```{r read-sheepdog, eval = FALSE}
x <- fp_read_sheepdog("occupancy_export", species = "compau")
auto <- fp_aggregate(x$occasions, x$detections, threshold = 0.5,
                     by = c("site", "occasion_id"), validation = x$validation)
```

## Building the occasions

The classifier lists detections only, so the occasions come from a table
of all recordings: here, one per site and night, with the site covariate.

```{r occasions}
occasions <- data.frame(site = truth$site, file = truth$file)
sites <- sim$data$sites
```

`fp_aggregate()` marks an occasion as a detection when it has a detection
at or above the threshold, and turns the verdicts into the counts `n_true`
and `n_false` of the occasions that were checked. Verdicts on clips below
the threshold are dropped, since those clips are not detections at this
threshold.

```{r aggregate}
auto <- fp_aggregate(occasions, detections, threshold = 0.5,
                     validation = verdicts)
head(auto)
c(detections = sum(auto$y), checked = sum(!is.na(auto$n_true)))
all(auto$y == truth$y)
```

The occasions are the same as in the simulated truth. `fp_aggregate()`
warns when an occasion has more detections at or above the threshold than
reviewed clips, because the confirmation design assumes that every detection
of a checked occasion was checked.

## Fitting the model

The result goes to `fp_data()` as the automated table, with the names of the
confirmation counts.

```{r fp-data}
d <- fp_data(auto, sites, confirmed = c("n_true", "n_false"))
d
```

```{r fit, eval = has_stan, message = FALSE}
m <- fp_occu(d, occ = ~ x, fp = ~ 1, random_recorder = FALSE,
             threads_per_chain = 1, seed = 1,
             refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE)
summary(m)
```

The simulation used an occupancy slope of `r sim$truth$b1` and a
false-positive rate of `r sim$truth$p10`; both lie inside the 95% intervals. The rest of the analysis, from
convergence checks to predictions, is the same as in `vignette("crywolf")`.

## With real files

Real data differ from this example in a few ways that matter.

* The occasion table must list every recording, including those where
  BirdNET found nothing, with the site and any covariates. A list of the
  audio files on disk is a good start.
* An occasion can be shorter than a file. With one-minute occasions, add a
  column for the minute to both tables and pass `by = c("file", "minute")`.
* BirdNET tables hold every species; give `species` to `fp_aggregate()` to
  keep one.
* The threshold changes which occasions are detections, and with them the
  estimates. `vignette("threshold")` shows how to check that.

## References

Chambert, T., Miller, D. A. W., & Nichols, J. D. (2015). Modeling false
positive detections in species occurrence data under different study
designs. *Ecology*, 96, 332–339. https://doi.org/10.1890/14-1507.1

Kahl, S., Wood, C. M., Eibl, M., & Klinck, H. (2021). BirdNET: A deep
learning solution for avian diversity monitoring. *Ecological Informatics*,
61, 101236. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecoinf.2021.101236

Miller, D. A., Nichols, J. D., McClintock, B. T., Grant, E. H. C., Bailey,
L. L., & Weir, L. A. (2011). Improving occupancy estimation when two types of
observational error occur: non-detection and species misidentification.
*Ecology*, 92, 1422–1428. https://doi.org/10.1890/10-1396.1
